day-1.t: Day 1 — Set up WhatsApp Business properly

b.v: Today's goal

v: Install the Business app and keep your normal number
Fill the profile so buyers trust you in one look
Set the greeting, away and quick answers

b.v: About 20 minutes. WhatsApp Business is free and separate from your normal WhatsApp.

Most buyers decide whether to trust a shop before they read a single reply. A complete profile with a real name, a real address and clear hours does that work silently. An empty profile with a random photo makes people ask for proof, and many do not bother asking.
1) Install and keep your number
WhatsApp Business is a separate app from WhatsApp. Both can live on the same phone with different numbers, but one number can only be active in one app at a time.

Set up:|Install WhatsApp Business from the app store|Register with the number your customers already have|Choose a business name people recognise, not a slogan|Add a logo or a clear product photo as the profile picture|Fill category, address, hours and a one-line description
2) The profile fields that earn trust
Write the profile for someone who has never heard of you and is deciding whether to send money.

v: Name: your shop name as customers say it, for example Al-Noor Fabrics
Description: what you sell, where you deliver, and how fast
Address: a real location, even a small one; buyers check this
Hours: when you actually reply, so people are not angry at 2 am
Catalogue: your products, with prices written as check today's price on the product card

b.v: 3) Turn on the three automatic messages
These answer the questions you get twenty times a day. Keep them short and human, and never let them make a promise you cannot keep.

@Greeting message
Assalam o alaikum and welcome to Al-Noor Fabrics. Thanks for messaging us.

You can see our full range in the catalogue. Tell me the item and your city, and I will confirm the price and delivery time.

We reply between 10 am and 8 pm, Monday to Saturday.
Do not use a shop name, logo or product photos copied from another brand. Buyers notice, and copied branding can get the business account reported and removed.
Practice

Complete every profile field today, add one real product to the catalogue and write your greeting message in your own words. Then send a test message to a friend to see how the profile looks to a stranger.

day-2.t: Day 2 — A catalogue that answers before you do

b.v: Today's goal

v: Add products with prices, photos and options
Write descriptions that answer size and material questions
Keep the catalogue short and current

b.v: About 25 minutes. You need five good photos of your five best sellers.
A catalogue is your shop window inside the chat. When it is good, half your questions disappear, and the buyer arrives at the price conversation already interested.
1) Photograph like a shop, not like a hobby
Buyers cannot touch the product, so the photo is the product. Daylight, one item, plain background, and a second photo showing the detail people ask about.

v: One item per photo, filling most of the frame
Daylight near a window, flash off
A plain bedsheet or wall behind, not the shop floor
A second close-up of stitching, label or size tag
Same angle for every product, so the catalogue looks like one shop

b.v: 2) What goes in each product card
The card has limited space. Put the three facts that decide the sale in the first line, and leave the details for the description.

@Product card
Name: Cotton kurta, unstitched
Price: check today's price, ask for the current rate
Description: 2.5 metres, 100 percent cotton, suited to Lahore summer. Available in white, grey and sky blue. Delivery in Lahore 1 to 2 days, other cities 3 to 5 days. Cash on delivery available up to Rs 5,000. Stitching not included.
3) Keep it current
An old price in the catalogue causes arguments you cannot win. Update the catalogue the same day a price changes, and remove sold-out items instead of leaving them to disappoint buyers.
Do not promise cash on delivery or a delivery date in the catalogue unless you can hold it every day. One broken promise in writing is quoted back to you by every buyer who reads it.
Practice
Photograph your five best sellers today and add them to the catalogue with a price, a short description and delivery information. Then ask one friend to read a card and tell you what is missing.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Quick replies and message templates

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write the eight replies that cover most chats
Save them so they take two taps
Edit every one before sending

b.v: About 25 minutes. Use real chats from the last week as your source.

Typing the same answer fifty times a day is how shop owners start replying late and then stop replying at all. Saved replies give you speed back, and speed is what keeps a buyer from ordering somewhere else.
1) The eight replies you actually need
Read your last fifty chats and count the repeated questions. Almost every shop needs these eight, in some wording.

v: Greeting and how can I help
Price and availability of one item
Size, colour and material details
Cash on delivery and advance payment terms
Delivery time and charges by city
Order confirmed, with what happens next
Order dispatched, with tracking
Out of stock, with an alternative

b.v: 2) How to save them
In WhatsApp Business you can store quick replies and call them with a short slash code while typing. Keep the codes short and memorable.

Save a quick reply:|Open Business settings, then Quick replies|Add a short code such as /price or /cod|Write the message with a blank where the name or item goes|Save and test it in a chat with yourself|Fix anything that sounds like a robot
3) Edit before you send, every time
A saved reply that says Dear customer when the person's name is on screen feels careless. Two seconds of editing is the difference between service and a machine.
Do not send the same long message to many numbers at once. Bulk unsolicited messages get the business number reported and restricted, and every chat you had is lost with it.
Practice
Write and save five of the eight replies today with your own prices and delivery times. Then use one in a real chat and see whether the buyer's next message is easier to answer.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Labels that stop you losing buyers

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create labels for the stages of an order
Clear the chat list every evening
Never lose an unanswered buyer again

b.v: About 20 minutes. Use this on today's real chats, not on old ones.
In a busy shop the chat list is your order book. When it is a wall of names with no order, buyers get missed. Labels turn the list into a simple pipeline you can read in thirty seconds.
1) Six labels, in the order of the sale
Name the labels as stages of money, not as people. Then you can always see where the money is stuck.

v: New — messaged, not answered yet
Quoted — price sent, waiting for a yes
Paid — payment received, needs dispatch
Dispatched — with the courier, tracking sent
Delivered — done, ask for a review later
Follow up — interested, not ready yet

b.v: 2) The evening clear-out
Ten minutes at closing time keeps the list honest. Anything without a label is something you forgot.

Evening routine:|Open the chat list and filter to New|Answer or quote every New chat|Label each one before you close it|Check Paid and make sure every parcel has a tracking number|Unlabel and archive Delivered chats older than a week
3) Use Follow up, but once
Most sales in a small shop happen on the second message. One polite follow-up two days later is service. Three is pressure, and pressure gets blocked.

@Follow up, two days later
Assalam o alaikum. Just checking whether you still want the grey kurta in medium — we have two left. If the timing is not right, no problem at all, message me whenever you are ready.
Do not label something Paid before the money is actually in your account or wallet. A screenshot of a transfer is not the money; check your own balance first.
Practice
Create the six labels now and apply them to every chat in your list. Then note how many were sitting in New without an answer — that number is what you were losing.

day-5.t: Day 5 — Tone that Pakistani buyers trust

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write in a warm, clear, short style
Handle Urdu, Roman Urdu and English in one chat
Stop using phrases that create distance

b.v: About 20 minutes. Rewrite three of your real replies at the end.
Buyers here do not judge you on perfect English. They judge you on whether you sound like a person who will actually send the parcel. Warmth plus clarity wins; formality plus vagueness loses.
1) Short lines, one idea each
Long paragraphs on a phone look like work. Break every message into two or three short lines and end with one clear question.

v: weak = Respected customer, we are extremely grateful for your kind inquiry and shall revert at the earliest
strong = Yes, we have it in medium. Price is Rs 2,400. Should I keep one for you?
weak = Kindly be informed that delivery may take some time
strong = Lahore gets it in 1 to 2 days. Other cities take 3 to 5 days.

b.v: 2) Match the buyer's language
If the buyer writes in Roman Urdu, answer in Roman Urdu. You do not need perfect spelling; you need to be understood and to sound like yourself.

@Roman Urdu replies
Price: Ji haan, yeh available hai. Price Rs 2,400 hai, delivery Lahore mein 1 se 2 din.
COD: COD Rs 5,000 tak available hai. Is se zyada order par advance dena hota hai.
Delay: Aap ka parcel kal dispatch ho gaya hai, tracking number shaam tak bhej deta hoon.
3) Words that create distance
Some words sound polite but read as cold or as a delay. Replace them with a fact or a time.

v: Kindly revert = please reply, or just ask the question
As per policy = here is what we do
Soon, shortly, some time = give a day or an hour
Dear customer = the person's name

b.v: Do not over-apologise in every message. Five sorries in one chat make the buyer nervous about the order, and nervous buyers cancel.
Practice
Take three real replies you sent this week and rewrite them with short lines, one question each, and no words from the list above. Compare which version you would answer faster as a buyer.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Price, COD and shipping questions

b.v: Today's goal

v: Answer price questions without discounting by reflex
Explain cash on delivery and advance payment clearly
Give delivery times you can keep

b.v: About 25 minutes. Know your real numbers before you start: cost, delivery charge, and COD limit.
Nearly every sale is decided in three questions: how much, can I pay on delivery, and when will it arrive. Clear answers close the sale. Vague answers send the buyer to the next shop.
1) Say the price once, then move forward
Give the number, what it includes, and the next step. Do not add sorry or a long explanation, and do not discount before the buyer asks.

@Price and value reply
Rs 2,400 for the kurta, including the matching dupatta.

Courier is Rs 200 in Lahore and Rs 350 outside. If you take two, I can send both in one parcel and you pay one courier charge.

Should I pack the grey one?
2) Cash on delivery, in one clear message
State the limit, the extra charge if any, and what you need from the buyer. A buyer who understands the rule stops arguing about it.

v: COD available up to Rs 5,000; above that a partial advance is needed
COD parcels are opened for checking before payment, if your courier allows it
Advance is taken by JazzCash, Easypaisa or bank transfer, and you send a receipt
Refused COD parcels cost you the delivery charge, so confirm the address once

b.v: 3) Delivery time by city, not by hope
Give a range based on your courier's real performance, and send the tracking number yourself rather than waiting to be asked.

v: Same city: 1 to 2 working days
Major cities: 3 to 5 working days
Small towns: 4 to 7 working days, and say so before the order
Friday and Sunday can slow things down; mention it when the date is tight

b.v: Do not promise next-day delivery outside your city to win an order. A late parcel costs you the sale, the courier charge and the review, and the buyer tells others.
Practice
Write your three standard replies for price, COD and delivery, with your real numbers filled in. Save them as quick replies and use one today.
Today's goal

v: Calm the chat in the first two replies
Separate the apology from the solution
Know when to refund and when to hold

b.v: About 20 minutes. Think of your worst real complaint as you read.

An angry buyer is not your enemy. They are a person who feels ignored and wants someone to take responsibility. Almost every complaint that becomes a public review became one because nobody answered properly in the first hour.
1) The four-step reply
Acknowledge, apologise once, state the fact, offer two options. Do it in that order, in short lines, and never argue about who is right in the first message.

@Angry customer, first reply
I understand why you are upset — you paid and the parcel has not arrived. I am sorry about that.

I checked: it left our shop on Tuesday and the courier shows it at their Lahore hub. It has been sitting there two days, which is their delay, not yours to solve.

Two options: I can call the courier now and push for delivery tomorrow, or I can send a replacement today by a different courier at our cost. Which do you prefer?
2) Rules that keep the chat calm
These four habits decide whether the buyer calms down or escalates.

v: Reply within the hour, even if only to say I am checking and will confirm by 4 pm
Never blame the courier as an excuse; say what you will do about it
Give a time for the next update, and keep it
Move the conversation to a call if the messages go in circles twice

b.v: 3) Refund or replace
Decide your policy before the argument, so the decision is not made in anger. Write it down and keep it short.

v: Wrong or damaged item: replace or refund, your choice, no argument
Late parcel still in transit: offer to wait with a firm date, or refund
Buyer changed their mind on a customised item: partial refund at most, stated in advance
Repeated free replacement requests from the same buyer: stop, politely, in writing

b.v: Do not delete a complaint, block the buyer, or reply with sarcasm, even if they are rude. Screenshots travel, and one bad screenshot in a Facebook group costs more than the refund.
Practice
Write your four-step angry customer reply with your own products, and write your refund policy in three lines. Save both where you can reach them during a busy day.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Order updates that prevent complaints

b.v: Today's goal

v: Send four updates at four fixed points
Write a tracking message people understand
Turn a delivered order into a repeat buyer

b.v: About 20 minutes. Set up the four messages as quick replies.
Most complaints are not about delays. They are about silence. A buyer who is told the parcel is late will wait. A buyer who is told nothing starts imagining the worst and writing reviews.
1) Four updates, four moments
Send them automatically at the same points for every order, so it becomes a habit rather than a decision.

v: Order received: what you got, the total, and when it is dispatched
Dispatched: courier name, tracking number, expected days
In transit, only if it is late: what happened and the new date
Delivered: confirm it arrived, and ask one question about the product

b.v: 2) The dispatch message
This is the message buyers screenshot and check. Put the tracking number on its own line so it is easy to copy.

@Dispatch message
Your order is on the way.

Courier: Leopards
Tracking: ________
Expected: 3 to 5 working days, so around Thursday

If nobody calls you from the courier in two days, message me and I will follow it up myself.
3) The delivered message that brings them back
Ask one specific question, not a generic one. A specific question gets answered, and the answer tells you what to stock next.
Do not send a tracking number you have not checked, and do not mark an order dispatched before the courier has it. A wrong tracking number creates more messages than sending none.
Practice
Save all four update messages as quick replies with blanks for the courier and tracking number. Then apply them to your next five orders and count how many buyers message you first.

day-9.t: Day 9 — Close the sale without pushing

b.v: Today's goal

v: Ask for the order in one clear line
Handle the three delays buyers use
Stop losing sales at the last message

b.v: About 20 minutes. Use one real chat that went quiet.
Many chats end with the buyer asking the price and never replying. Usually nobody asked for the order. A shop that answers questions but never asks for the sale leaves money in the chat.
1) One clear closing line
The closing line names the item, the next step and a small choice. It is not pressure; it is help making a decision.

v: Should I pack the grey one in medium for you?
Do you want it delivered to your home or your office address?
I can hold one until tomorrow evening — shall I?

b.v: 2) The three delays, and what to do
Buyers rarely say no. They say later, or expensive, or I will check. Each one has a different answer.
3) When to let it go
Not every chat becomes an order. One follow-up, then stop and label it Follow up. A buyer who feels chased stops replying, and a buyer who feels helped comes back.
Do not create false urgency, such as claiming only one piece is left when you have twenty. Buyers check, and a shop caught inventing scarcity loses the sale and the customer.
Practice
Write your closing line and the three delay replies in your own words. Then send your closing line in one real chat that has gone quiet, and note the result.

day-10.t: Day 10 — Privacy, records, and when to call

b.v: Today's goal

v: Keep customer data safe and your records clean
Know when a chat should become a call
Set a simple rule for what you never send

b.v: About 20 minutes. Check who else has access to your shop phone today.

Your chat list is a list of names, addresses, phone numbers and often payment screenshots. It is the most valuable thing your shop owns, and the easiest to leak. Good records also make you money, because you can see what actually sells.
1) Protect the data you already hold
Basic habits stop almost every problem, and none of them cost money.

v: Keep the shop phone locked, and never share the verification code with anyone
Do not forward a customer's address or number to another customer
Delete card photos and transfer screenshots after you record them
Remove access for staff who have left, the same day
Never post a screenshot of a chat without hiding the name and number

b.v: 2) A record of every order
Keep one sheet, not a pile of screenshots. Five columns are enough to run a small shop and to answer a complaint months later.

@Order sheet columns
Date | Buyer name and number | Item, size, colour | Amount and payment method | Courier and tracking | Status
3) When to move the chat to a call
Typing is slow for complicated problems. A two-minute call beats forty messages, and buyers calm down faster when they hear a voice.

v: Move to a call: address confusion, repeated delivery failure, a complaint after two rounds, a bulk order
Stay in chat: prices, sizes, stock, tracking numbers, anything the buyer may need in writing
Always send a short written summary after the call, so the agreement exists in the chat

b.v: Do not call a buyer at night or repeatedly after they do not answer. One call at a reasonable hour, then a message: I tried calling, tell me a good time and I will call you.
Practice
Build your order sheet with the six columns and enter your last ten orders. Then write the one-line rule you will use before sending any screenshot, and keep it as a saved note on your phone.
